subject: physics
title: Work done
key_idea: **Work done** is the energy transferred when a force moves an object. Work done equals force times distance moved in the direction of the force. One joule is one newton-metre. Work done against friction heats the object.

blocks.text: When a force makes an object move, the force does work on it. This section covers what work is and how to measure it.

items.meaning: The energy transferred when a force moves an object through a distance.
The unit of work and energy. One joule is the work done when a force of one newton moves an object one metre.
Another name for the joule: 1 J = 1 N m.

items: A force does work only when the object moves.
Energy transferred and work done are equal, and both are measured in joules.
Lifting a weight, pushing a trolley and braking a car all involve work done.
Work is done when a force causes a displacement of an object.
Work done is the energy transferred, in joules.
1 joule = 1 newton-metre.

blocks.text: The distance used must be along the line of the force.

blocks.label: Work done
where: W is work done in joules (J).
s is distance moved along the line of action of the force in metres (m).

items.text: Change any distance in centimetres to metres. 86 cm = 0.86 m.
A force of 3.0 N moves a trolley 0.86 m: W = 3.0 × 0.86
W = 2.58 J, which is 2.6 J to 2 significant figures.

blocks.text: Move the sliders to see how the force and distance change the work done.

diagram.alt: Change a force and a distance to see the work done.
Calculate work done with a distance in centimetres.
diagram.question: A force of {F} N moves a trolley {d} cm along a desk. Calculate the work done in joules.

items: Measure the pulling force with a force meter (newton meter).
Measure the distance moved with a ruler or metre rule.
Repeat with different masses on the block, then use work done = force × distance.

blocks.label: Rearranged to find force or distance
blocks.formula: F = W ÷ s and s = W ÷ F
where: W is work done in joules (J).

items: W = F × s, with distance in metres and force in newtons.
Always give the unit: J or N m.
Rearrange the equation to find a force or a distance.

blocks.text: Friction and air resistance oppose motion. Work done against them transfers energy to the surroundings.

items: Work done against friction raises the temperature of the object.
When a car brakes, friction in the brakes does work. Kinetic energy is transferred to the thermal store of the brakes.
A cyclist or wheelchair racer does work against air resistance. The energy comes from their chemical store.

blocks.text: Work done by forces also changes energy stores. This links work done to energy transfers.

items: Lifting an object does work against gravity and raises its gravitational potential energy store.
A landing spacecraft has work done on it by gravity, by its thrusters and by air resistance on the parachute. Its kinetic energy store decreases and its thermal store increases.

blocks.text: (Physics only) The work done to bring a vehicle to rest equals its initial kinetic energy. For a constant braking force, this shows how braking distance depends on speed.

blocks.label: Work done to stop a vehicle
where: F is braking force in newtons (N).
s is braking distance in metres (m).
v is initial speed in metres per second (m/s).

items: Braking distance s is proportional to v².
Doubling the speed makes the braking distance four times as long.
Work done against friction heats the object and its surroundings.
The kinetic energy of a braking vehicle becomes thermal energy in the brakes.
(Physics only) Work done in stopping equals initial kinetic energy, so braking distance depends on speed squared.

checks.q: A force of 5600 N brings a car to a stop in 20 m. Calculate the work done by the brakes, with its unit.
A trolley is moved 86 cm by a force of 3.0 N. Calculate the work done to 2 significant figures.
Explain why braking increases the temperature of the brakes.
checks.a: Work is done by friction in the brakes. Some kinetic energy of the vehicle is transferred as thermal energy in the brakes.

worked_example.question:
The distance of the London Marathon is 42 000 m.
During the race, wheelchair competitors work against air resistance.
The work done against air resistance by the winner of the race was 3 360 000 J.

Calculate the average air resistance acting on the winner of the race.
worked_example.tip: One mark for the substitution, one for the rearrangement and one for the answer.

worked_example.question:
A force of 1200 N pulls a truck along a horizontal road for a distance of 8.0 m.

Calculate the work done by the 1200 N force.
Use the equation: work done = force × distance moved in the direction of the force

State the unit of work done.
worked_example.tip: The unit is an independent mark. J, joule(s) and N m are all accepted.

worked_example.question:
A trolley moves a distance of 86 cm along a desk.

Calculate the work done when a force of 3.0 N is applied.
Use the equation: work done = force × distance

Give your answer to 2 significant figures.
worked_example.tip: A correct answer of 2.6 J scores all 4 marks. A missing unit conversion can still earn marks for the working.

worked_example.question:
An archer pulls back on the bow string, doing a total of 110 J of work. Her hand moves a distance of 0.45 m. The bow is bent and stores energy.

Show that the average force applied by the archer in pulling the string back is approximately 240 N.
answer_points: W = F × d, so F = W ÷ d
F = 110 ÷ 0.45 = 244 N, which is about 240 N
worked_example.tip: One mark for the equation and one mark for the value of 244 N.

blocks.text: Work done is also written W = Fd, where d is the distance moved (s in the equation above).

items: Mechanical work done = F × d.
Work done = energy transferred, so W = Fd = ΔE, where ΔE is the change in energy.
Electrical work done is also equal to the energy transferred.

worked_example.question:
A winch is used to pull a truck along a horizontal road.
The winch does 41 kJ of useful work on the truck when the truck is pulled a horizontal distance of 15 m.

Calculate the force that the rope exerts on the truck.
worked_example.tip: One mark each for substitution, rearrangement and evaluation. Forgetting to convert kJ to J loses a mark.

blocks.text: Conservation of energy links work done, gravitational potential energy and kinetic energy.

items: Lifting a load at a steady speed: work done by the lifting force = gain in gravitational potential energy.
A force speeding up an object: work done = gain in kinetic energy.
A falling object with no energy dissipated: gravitational potential energy lost = kinetic energy gained.
